0	# PubMedChat Prototype Implementation Plan
1	
2	**Status:** Prototype planning / ready for implementation  
3	**Owner:** Project maintainer  
4	**Last updated:** 2026-08-13  
5	**Canonical path:** `docs/pubmedchat-prototype-implementation-plan.md`
6	
7	> **Implementation handoff:** Read this document before implementing PubMedChat prototype work. Treat the milestones and acceptance criteria as the implementation contract. If the existing repository differs from this plan, preserve working repository conventions, document the deviation in the Decision Log, and avoid silently changing scope.
8	
9	## 1. Objective
10	
11	Build a WikiChat-style, citation-first research assistant over PubMed-indexed abstracts. A user should be able to ask a biomedical literature question, receive a concise synthesis grounded in retrieved abstracts, inspect the supporting papers and excerpts, and understand the limits of the evidence.
12	
13	The prototype is a **literature discovery and summarization tool**, not a clinical decision-support system or medical adviser.
14	
15	### Success looks like
16	
17	- A user enters a research question in natural language.
18	- PubMed records are searched and ranked using a reproducible local or fixture-backed index.
19	- The system returns a grounded answer with PMID-level citations beside substantive claims.
20	- Each citation opens an inspectable source card with title, journal, date, PMID, PubMed URL, and supporting abstract text.
21	- The system clearly handles no results, insufficient evidence, conflicting findings, API failures, and unsafe personalized-medical questions.
22	- The prototype can be run locally with documented commands and without committed secrets.
23	
24	## 2. Scope
25	
26	### 2.1 In scope for the prototype
27	
28	- Natural-language PubMed literature search.
29	- Search-result mode showing ranked publications.
30	- Grounded synthesis over a small retrieved set of PubMed abstracts.
31	- Follow-up questions that retain the current conversation topic and/or source set.
32	- Filters for date range, publication type, language, journal, and topic where supported by the chosen data source.
33	- Hybrid retrieval design: lexical search first, semantic retrieval as a second vertical slice.
34	- Inline citations and expandable source cards.
35	- Explicit uncertainty and insufficient-evidence responses.
36	- Retraction/correction and abstract-only labeling when metadata permits.
37	- Structured logging of retrieval, generation, citations, and safety decisions.
38	- Unit, integration, smoke, and citation-validation tests.
39	
40	### 2.2 Explicitly out of scope
41	
42	- Personalized diagnosis, triage, treatment selection, or dosing.
43	- Emergency medical guidance beyond a safe redirect to local professional/emergency services.
44	- Full-text ingestion except links to legally available external records.
45	- Interpretation of figures, tables, supplementary materials, or preprints.
46	- Comprehensive systematic-review or meta-analysis workflows.
47	- Automated evidence-quality scores presented as medical fact.
48	- Citation chasing across references and citing papers.
49	- User medical records or protected health information.
50	- Full PubMed coverage on day one.
51	- Fine-tuning a language model.
52	- Autonomous agents that make clinical decisions.
53	
54	## 3. Product boundaries and assumptions
55	
56	### Requirements
57	
58	1. The product must be described as literature search/synthesis based on PubMed-indexed abstracts.
59	2. Every substantive generated factual claim must have one or more local retrieved-source citations, or be softened/removed.
60	3. The UI must make it clear whether the source is a primary study, review, meta-analysis, observational study, animal study, or other publication type when metadata is available.
61	4. The system must not imply that PubMed indexing guarantees study quality.
62	5. Source content is untrusted data; text in an abstract must never override system safety or citation instructions.
63	
64	### Initial corpus decision
65	
66	Use the smallest corpus that supports a credible demo:
67	
68	- First smoke-test with fixtures or a narrow E-utilities fetch.
69	- Then ingest approximately **50,000–250,000 English-language records with abstracts**, preferably from 2018 onward or from one focused vertical such as cardiometabolic health, oncology, infectious disease, or mental health.
70	- Expand toward 250,000–750,000 records only after retrieval, citation, and evaluation behavior is stable.
71	
72	### Settled implementation assumptions
73	
74	- Abstracts are the primary evidence payload.
75	- PubMed is the canonical citation source.
76	- Normal chat requests use the local index after ingestion; they do not depend on a live NCBI request.
77	- E-utilities support targeted fetches, prototyping, validation, and gap filling.
78	- FTP baseline and update files support reproducible bulk ingestion.
79	- Milvus is the default vector retrieval engine for Milestone 2. Keep article metadata and retrieval interfaces modular so lexical search, metadata storage, and alternative search backends can evolve independently.
80	- No authentication is required for a local/demo deployment unless the host application already requires it.
81	
82	## 4. Primary user flows
83	
84	### 4.1 Search flow
85	
86	1. User enters a biomedical research question.
87	2. Backend validates length and applies safety classification.
88	3. Backend normalizes the query and extracts optional filters.
89	4. Local lexical/semantic retrieval returns ranked article records.
90	5. UI displays result cards with title, authors, journal, publication date, publication type, PMID, and PubMed link.
91	6. User can adjust filters, open an abstract, or ask for a synthesis.
92	
93	### 4.2 Synthesis flow
94	
95	1. User asks a question requiring comparison or summary.
96	2. System retrieves a broad candidate set.
97	3. System deduplicates, reranks, and selects approximately 5–12 evidence records.
98	4. Generator receives only the selected records/excerpts plus explicit citation IDs.
99	5. Citation validator checks that cited PMIDs exist and snippets come from the cited records.
100	6. UI streams or displays the answer with inline citations, caveats, search scope, and sources.
101	
102	### 4.3 Follow-up flow
103	
104	1. User asks a follow-up question.
105	2. System retains the conversation topic, prior filters, and optionally the prior source set.
106	3. System must still perform fresh retrieval when the follow-up changes the evidence question or asks for recent literature.
107	4. The response identifies whether it uses the prior source set, fresh sources, or both.
108	
109	### 4.4 Empty, insufficient, and failure states
110	
111	- **No results:** explain the search scope and suggest relaxing filters or trying synonyms.
112	- **Insufficient evidence:** say that the indexed abstracts do not support a reliable answer; show the closest sources only if useful.
113	- **Conflicting evidence:** summarize the disagreement and identify study designs/populations rather than forcing a single conclusion.
114	- **NCBI/API failure:** serve local results when possible; otherwise show a recoverable error and do not fabricate sources.
115	- **Malformed record:** skip it, log it, and continue ingestion.
116	- **Unsafe personal-health request:** provide a concise safe redirect rather than ordinary RAG output.
117	
118	## 5. Proposed architecture
119	
120	```text
121	                +-------------------+
122	                |  React/Next.js UI  |
123	                +---------+---------+
124	                          |
125	                    REST/stream API
126	                          |
127	                +---------v---------+
128	                |   API/orchestrator |
129	                | query + safety     |
130	                +----+----------+----+
131	                     |          |
132	          +----------v--+   +---v-------------+
133	          | Retrieval    |   | Answer generator |
134	          | lexical      |   | citation-aware  |
135	          | semantic     |   +---+-------------+
136	          | fusion/rank  |       |
137	          +------+-------+   +---v-------------+
138	                 |           | Citation check  |
139	                 |           +-----------------+
140	        +--------v------------------+
141	        |  Article metadata store     |
142	        |  + Milvus vector indexes    |
143	        +--------+------------------+
144	                 |
145	        +--------v------------------+
146	        | Object storage: raw XML/API |
147	        +-----------------------------+
148	
149	  Background workers: FTP download, parse, normalize, embed, index, updates
150	  External sources: NCBI PubMed FTP and E-utilities; LLM/embedding provider
151	```
152	
153	### Component responsibilities
154	
155	- **Web UI:** chat/search input, filters, ranked results, answer rendering, citation cards, loading/error states, feedback.
156	- **API/orchestrator:** request validation, query classification, retrieval orchestration, answer generation, citation validation, response shaping.
157	- **Safety service:** classify high-risk personalized-medical requests and apply refusal/redirect policy before generation.
158	- **Ingestion workers:** download and checksum FTP files, parse XML as a stream, normalize records, process updates/deletions, and enqueue embeddings/indexing.
159	- **Retrieval service:** lexical search, vector search, rank fusion, deduplication, reranking, metadata filters, and diversification.
160	- **Generation service:** produce structured answers from selected evidence only.
161	- **Citation validator:** verify PMID existence, citation-to-record mapping, supporting excerpts, and unsupported claims where feasible.
162	- **Article metadata store:** canonical records, versions, traces, benchmark data, and application state; start with the smallest practical local store and introduce PostgreSQL only if needed for durability and query complexity.
163	- **Milvus:** vector collections for title/abstract embeddings, scalar metadata needed for retrieval filters, index parameters, and corpus-versioned retrieval experiments.
164	- **Object storage:** immutable raw FTP XML, API payloads, manifests, and processing reports.
165	
166	## 6. PubMed ingestion requirements
167	
168	### 6.1 E-utilities prototype path
169	
170	Implement this first if the repository is empty or time-to-demo is the priority:
171	
172	- Use `ESearch` to identify PMIDs.
173	- Use `EFetch` in batches to retrieve XML records.
174	- Cache responses.
175	- Configure the required NCBI `tool` and contact email.
176	- Respect NCBI request limits and retry transient errors with backoff.
177	- Persist normalized records locally so chat does not call the API on every turn.
178	
179	### 6.2 FTP bulk path
180	
181	Implement after the first vertical slice:
182	
183	1. Download PubMed baseline archives and checksums.
184	2. Store immutable raw files.
185	3. Parse XML incrementally; do not load an archive into memory.
186	4. Normalize records by PMID.
187	5. Filter according to corpus criteria.
188	6. Upsert articles idempotently.
189	7. Build lexical documents and enqueue embedding jobs.
190	8. Process update and deletion files on a daily or weekly schedule.
191	9. Retain source filename/release, checksum, parser version, and timestamps.
192	
193	### 6.3 Article schema
194	
195	Minimum normalized fields:
196	
197	- `pmid`
198	- `title`
199	- `abstract_text`
200	- `abstract_sections`
201	- `authors`
202	- `journal`
203	- `issn`
204	- `doi`
205	- `pmc_id`
206	- electronic/print/PubMed publication dates
207	- `language`
208	- `publication_types`
209	- `mesh_terms`
210	- `keywords`
211	- correction/retraction flags
212	- `source_release`
213	- `content_hash`
214	- `first_seen_at`
215	- `last_updated_at`
216	- `active`
217	
218	Do not discard records solely because an abstract is missing; retain them as metadata-only records but exclude them from synthesis retrieval unless explicitly requested.
219	
220	## 7. Retrieval and RAG requirements
221	
222	### 7.1 Query classification and normalization
223	
224	Classify requests as search, synthesis, comparison, explanation, fact lookup, unsafe personal-health request, or emergency/high-risk request. Preserve the original query. Extract entities, population, intervention, comparator, outcome, date range, study type, human/animal constraints, and likely MeSH/synonym expansions.
225	
226	### 7.2 Candidate retrieval
227	
228	- Lexical retrieval over title, abstract, MeSH, and publication metadata.
229	- Dense retrieval over title plus abstract.
230	- Metadata filters for date, language, journal, publication type, and topic.
231	- Retrieve approximately 50–100 candidates per retrieval route.
232	- Merge by reciprocal-rank fusion or a documented weighted score.
233	- Deduplicate by PMID, DOI, and near-identical titles.
234	- Rerank the top 30–50 candidates.
235	- Select approximately 5–12 sources for synthesis.
236	- Diversify by study design, publication date, and journal where appropriate.
237	
238	### 7.3 Grounded generation contract
239	
240	The generator must:
241	
242	- receive only selected source excerpts and metadata;
243	- use stable citation IDs mapped to PMIDs;
244	- cite each substantive claim at sentence or clause level;
245	- avoid inventing numerical results or full-text details;
246	- use association/causal language appropriate to study design;
247	- distinguish review from primary evidence;
248	- identify mixed findings and important limitations;
249	- state when evidence is insufficient.
250	
251	Suggested response object:
252	
253	```json
254	{
255	  "answer_markdown": "...",
256	  "claims": [
257	    {
258	      "text": "...",
259	      "citation_ids": ["src_1", "src_2"]
260	    }
261	  ],
262	  "citations": [
263	    {
264	      "id": "src_1",
265	      "pmid": "12345678",
266	      "title": "...",
267	      "journal": "...",
268	      "publication_date": "2024-01-01",
269	      "publication_types": ["Randomized Controlled Trial"],
270	      "pubmed_url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678/",
271	      "supporting_excerpt": "..."
272	    }
273	  ],
274	  "limitations": ["Abstract-only evidence"],
275	  "search_scope": {
276	    "retrieved_at": "...",
277	    "filters": {}
278	  },
279	  "safety": {
280	    "classification": "literature_question",
281	    "redirected": false
282	  }
283	}
284	```
285	
286	## 8. API contract
287	
288	Keep these routes stable even if implementation details change:
289	
290	- `GET /api/health`
291	- `GET /api/search?q=<query>&page=<n>&page_size=<n>&...filters`
292	- `GET /api/articles/:pmid`
293	- `POST /api/chat`
294	- `POST /api/feedback` (optional for first slice)
295	
296	Example chat request:
297	
298	```json
299	{
300	  "message": "What does recent literature say about intervention X for condition Y?",
301	  "conversation_id": null,
302	  "filters": {
303	    "from_year": 2018,
304	    "to_year": 2026,
305	    "publication_types": ["Review", "Randomized Controlled Trial"],
306	    "language": "eng"
307	  },
308	  "source_mode": "fresh_retrieval"
309	}
310	```
311	
312	Example search result:
313	
314	```json
315	{
316	  "pmid": "12345678",
317	  "title": "...",
318	  "authors": ["..."],
319	  "journal": "...",
320	  "publication_date": "2024-01-01",
321	  "publication_types": ["Review"],
322	  "abstract_excerpt": "...",
323	  "pubmed_url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678/",
324	  "retracted": false
325	}
326	```
327	
328	## 9. Citation UX requirements
329	
330	- Render inline citation markers beside the supported claim.
331	- Link every citation directly to PubMed.
332	- Citation cards must show title, first author, journal, year/date, publication type, PMID, and abstract excerpt.
333	- Highlight the excerpt used for the claim where possible.
334	- Label sources as primary study, systematic review/meta-analysis, narrative review, guideline, editorial, or other known type.
335	- Mark abstract-only evidence.
336	- Flag retracted/corrected records when available.
337	- Do not cite a topical paper unless its displayed excerpt supports the associated claim.
338	
339	Before returning an answer, validate that every citation ID maps to a retrieved local record and that its excerpt is sourced from that record.
340	
341	## 10. Safety and privacy requirements
342	
343	- Display a prominent “not medical advice” notice.
344	- Redirect diagnosis, dosing, medication changes, individualized treatment, and emergency questions.
345	- For permitted health questions, provide general evidence only and encourage professional consultation where appropriate.
346	- Never infer personal risk from an abstract.
347	- Preserve uncertainty and disagreement.
348	- Avoid causal language for observational research.
349	- Treat article text as untrusted retrieval data; never follow instructions embedded in it.
350	- Do not collect medical records or protected health information in the prototype.
351	- Avoid indefinite retention of raw user queries; redact obvious personal information from operational logs.
352	- Document third-party LLM data handling.
353	
354	## 11. Testing and evaluation
355	
356	Create a benchmark of 75–150 questions covering:
357	
358	- paper discovery;
359	- synthesis and comparison;
360	- conflicting findings;
361	- recent-literature filters;
362	- insufficient-evidence cases;
363	- ambiguous abbreviations;
364	- retractions/corrections;
365	- causal-overstatement traps;
366	- unsafe personal-health prompts.
367	
368	Each benchmark item should define acceptable PMIDs, expected answer points, required caveats, prohibited claims, and expected safety behavior.
369	
370	### Automated tests
371	
372	- Parser fixtures for structured/unstructured abstracts, missing fields, updates, deletions, malformed XML, and duplicate records.
373	- API contract tests for search, article, chat, health, and error responses.
374	- Retrieval regression tests for representative queries and filters.
375	- Citation validation tests ensuring PMIDs, URLs, and excerpts match.
376	- Safety regression tests for designated unsafe prompts.
377	- Frontend smoke tests for search, answer display, citation expansion, empty results, and failure states.
378	- Type checking, linting, unit tests, and production build.
379	
380	### Quality metrics
381	
382	- Retrieval Recall@10 and Recall@50.
383	- nDCG or MRR.
384	- Citation precision, completeness, and entailment.
385	- Broken/mismatched citation rate.
386	- Unsupported substantive claim rate.
387	- Correct study-design and uncertainty handling.
388	- Correct abstention/refusal rate.
389	- p50/p95 latency, ingestion freshness, API failure rate, and cost per query.
390	
391	Human biomedical review is required for a launch sample. LLM-based grading may assist but is not the final scientific authority.
392	
393	## 12. Implementation milestones
394	
395	### Milestone 0 — repository and contract
396	
397	**Tasks**
398	
399	- Inspect existing repository conventions and runtime.
400	- Add environment-variable documentation without secrets.
401	- Add a health endpoint and test command.
402	- Create the canonical schemas and error format.
403	
404	**Acceptance criteria**
405	
406	- Local setup and test commands are documented.
407	- `GET /api/health` returns a stable success response.
408	- No secrets are committed.
409	
410	### Milestone 1 — PubMed search vertical slice
411	
412	**Tasks**
413	
414	- Implement E-utilities adapter with timeout, retry, cache, and rate-limit handling.
415	- Normalize fetched records.
416	- Add local fixture mode for offline tests.
417	- Implement `GET /api/search` and `GET /api/articles/:pmid`.
418	- Build ranked result cards and abstract view.
419	
420	**Acceptance criteria**
421	
422	- A representative query returns records containing PMID, title, journal, publication date, publication type when available, abstract excerpt, and PubMed URL.
423	- Fixture mode works without network access.
424	- Empty results and upstream failures have distinct, user-readable responses.
425	
426	### Milestone 2 — local index and retrieval
427	
428	**Tasks**
429	
430	- Add a Milvus collection schema for article or abstract-chunk embeddings keyed by PMID and corpus version.
431	- Add a small canonical metadata store for article records and retrieval traces.
432	- Add lexical indexing and metadata filters, with filter fields mirrored into Milvus when practical.
433	- Add chunking and embedding job interfaces that upsert vectors into Milvus idempotently.
434	- Add Milvus index/search configuration for local development and documented defaults.
435	- Add rank fusion, deduplication, and optional reranking across lexical and Milvus vector candidates.
436	
437	**Acceptance criteria**
438	
439	- The same query with the same corpus/version produces reproducible candidate rankings within documented tie behavior.
440	- Filters work and are covered by tests.
441	- Retrieval traces record query, corpus version, Milvus collection/index version, candidates, scores, and applied filters.
442	
443	### Milestone 3 — grounded chat
444	
445	**Tasks**
446	
447	- Implement query classification and safety routing.
448	- Implement `POST /api/chat`.
449	- Pass selected excerpts to a citation-aware generator.
450	- Validate citation IDs and source excerpts before response.
451	- Return structured answer, citations, limitations, search scope, and safety metadata.
452	
453	**Acceptance criteria**
454	
455	- Every substantive factual answer claim has a citation or an explicit uncertainty statement.
456	- No citation points to a PMID not retrieved for that answer.
457	- The model cannot cite a source absent from the supplied evidence context.
458	- Insufficient evidence produces an abstention rather than invented content.
459	
460	### Milestone 4 — citation-first UI
461	
462	**Tasks**
463	
464	- Add inline citations and citation cards.
465	- Show supporting abstract excerpts.
466	- Add filter controls and search-scope display.
467	- Add loading, empty, error, and unsafe-request states.
468	- Add follow-up conversation behavior.
469	
470	**Acceptance criteria**
471	
472	- A user can navigate from each material claim to its supporting PubMed record and excerpt.
473	- The UI clearly labels abstract-only evidence and study type where available.
474	- The user can recover from an empty result or transient error.
475	
476	### Milestone 5 — FTP ingestion and updates
477	
478	**Tasks**
479	
480	- Add FTP baseline downloader and checksum verification.
481	- Stream-parse baseline XML.
482	- Store manifests and raw artifacts.
483	- Add idempotent update/deletion processing.
484	- Add scheduled worker execution and ingestion reports.
485	
486	**Acceptance criteria**
487	
488	- A baseline subset can be reprocessed without duplicate articles or chunks.
489	- Update and deletion fixtures produce the expected active/inactive records.
490	- Failed records are isolated and reported without stopping the whole job.
491	
492	### Milestone 6 — verification and demo hardening
493	
494	**Tasks**
495	
496	- Create and run the benchmark suite.
497	- Review a sample with a biomedical domain expert.
498	- Test outdated, contradictory, retracted, missing-abstract, prompt-injection, and unsafe cases.
499	- Add latency, cost, error, and retrieval observability.
500	- Deploy a shareable demo with corpus date and limitations visible.
501	
502	**Acceptance criteria**
503	
504	- Unit, integration, smoke, type, lint, and build checks pass.
505	- Citation correctness and safety regression suites pass.
506	- A human-reviewed launch sample meets agreed quality thresholds.
507	- No known critical failure remains untracked.
508

555	## 14. Configuration
556	
557	Document names and purposes only. Never commit values:
558	
559	- `PUBMED_EMAIL` — contact email sent to NCBI.
560	- `PUBMED_TOOL` — application identifier sent to NCBI.
561	- `PUBMED_API_KEY` — optional NCBI API key.
562	- `PUBMED_BASE_URL` — configurable NCBI endpoint.
563	- `DATABASE_URL` — optional canonical metadata-store connection string when a database-backed store is used.
564	- `MILVUS_URI` — Milvus or Zilliz endpoint for vector retrieval.
565	- `MILVUS_TOKEN` — optional Milvus or Zilliz authentication token.
566	- `MILVUS_COLLECTION` — collection name for PubMed article or chunk embeddings.
567	- `MILVUS_DATABASE` — optional Milvus logical database name.
568	- `VECTOR_DIMENSION` — embedding vector dimension expected by the Milvus collection.
569	- `OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET` — raw input/artifact bucket.
570	- `OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT` — optional S3-compatible endpoint.
571	- `LLM_API_KEY` — model-provider credential.
572	- `LLM_MODEL` — generation model identifier.
573	- `EMBEDDING_MODEL` — embedding model identifier.
574	- `RERANKER_MODEL` — optional reranker identifier.
575	- `CACHE_URL` — optional cache/queue connection.
576	- `LOG_LEVEL` — application log level.
577	- `APP_ENV` — local, staging, or production.
578	
579	## 15. Local commands to document
580	
581	The implementation must provide repository-appropriate commands for:
582	
583	```text
584	install dependencies
585	start local services
586	run API
587	run web UI
588	run database migrations
589	ingest fixture data
590	run tests
591	run lint
592	run type checks
593	run production build
594	```
595	
596	Do not assume these exact commands if the repository already has conventions; document the actual commands in the project README after implementation.
597	
598	## 16. Risks and mitigations
599	
600	| Risk | Mitigation |
601	|---|---|
602	| PubMed rate limits or outage | Local cache/index, throttling, retries, fixture mode |
603	| Large FTP files | Streaming parser, resumable jobs, raw-file manifests |
604	| Embedding cost | Begin with bounded corpus; batch jobs; version embeddings |
605	| Hallucinated claims | Selected-source-only generation, structured claims, citation validation |
606	| Causal overstatement | Study-type metadata and generation policy |
607	| Conflicting literature | Diversified retrieval and explicit disagreement section |
608	| Retractions/corrections | Preserve and surface status flags |
609	| Abstract lacks needed detail | Explicit abstract-only limitation and abstention |
